Skill index from total and share trends

Source: R/trend_index.R
compose_skill_index.Rd

Builds, for each skill, the index of the skill stock as the product of the trend of the total stock and the trend of the skill share, source by source, then aggregates over sources with fixed weights.

Usage

compose_skill_index(
  total_tr,
  share_tr,
  source_col,
  skill_col,
  time_col,
  weights,
  base_period,
  min_covered = 0.5,
  scale = 100,
  value_col = "trend",
  cap = NULL,
  type = c("geometric", "arithmetic")
)

Arguments

total_tr

Trends of the total by source: columns source_col, time_col and value_col (log scale), e.g. from extract_trend() with transform = "log".

share_tr

Trends of skill shares by source: columns source_col, skill_col, time_col and value_col (logit scale), e.g. from extract_trend() with transform = "logit".

source_col

Name of the source column.

skill_col

Name of the skill column.

time_col

Name of the time column.

weights

A data.frame with columns source_col and w.

base_period

Two dates (start, end, inclusive) or the name of a logical column of share_tr.

min_covered

Minimum covered weight for a skill to be kept (in [0, 1]).

scale

Value of the index in the base period (default 100).

value_col

Name of the trend column in both tables (default "trend").

cap

NULL or the maximum weight of a source (see aggregate_index()).

type

Aggregation across sources: "geometric" (default) or "arithmetic" (see aggregate_index()).

Value

A data.table with columns skill_col, time_col, indice, n_sources, covered_weight and n_eff. Attributes: by_source (columns source_col, skill_col, time_col, log_trend, indice: per-source skill indices, input of index_jackknife()) and dropped (skills below min_covered, with covered_weight and n_sources).

Details

For source s, skill k and week t, the log trend of the skill stock is \(L_{s,k,t} = \tau_{s,t} + \log \mathrm{plogis}(\eta_{s,k,t})\), with \(\tau\) the log trend of the total and \(\eta\) the logit trend of the share. The per-source index is scale * exp(L - mean(L in base)) (geometric base, as in trend_index() with transform = "log"), so it factorises exactly as I_total * I_share / scale, where I_total is the geometric-base index of \(\tau\) and I_share the geometric-base index of log(plogis(eta)). Note that trend_index() with transform = "logit" uses an arithmetic base on shares, which differs from the geometric one by a constant factor per cell.

A cell (source, skill) is modelled when it has a non-missing index. The coverage of a skill is the share of the total weight held by its modelled sources; skills with coverage below min_covered are dropped and listed in the attribute dropped. The remaining skills are aggregated over sources with aggregate_index() rules: weights renormalised over the modelled sources in each week, optional cap. With type = "geometric" (default) the skill index is \(\exp(\sum_s \tilde w_s \log I_{s,k,t})\); with type = "arithmetic" it is \(\sum_s \tilde w_s I_{s,k,t}\), with \(\tilde w_s\) the weights renormalised over the sources whose cell (source, skill) is modelled in week t. The per-source indices (attribute by_source) do not depend on type. The exact factorisation total x share holds source by source; after aggregation it holds only for the geometric mean.

Examples

weeks <- data.table::as.IDate("2024-01-01") + 7L * (0:103)
tot <- data.table::data.table(
  source = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 104), week = rep(weeks, 2),
  trend = c(5 + 0.002 * (1:104), 4 + 0.001 * (1:104))
)
sh <- data.table::data.table(
  source = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 104), skill = "k1",
  week = rep(weeks, 2), trend = stats::qlogis(0.1 + 0.0005 * (1:208))
)
w <- data.table::data.table(source = c("a", "b"), w = c(2, 1))
compose_skill_index(tot, sh, "source", "skill", "week", w,
  base_period = c("2024-01-01", "2024-12-31")
)
#>       skill       week    indice n_sources covered_weight n_eff
#>      <char>     <IDat>     <num>     <int>          <num> <num>
#>   1:     k1 2024-01-01  86.08609         2              1   1.8
#>   2:     k1 2024-01-08  86.60990         2              1   1.8
#>   3:     k1 2024-01-15  87.13517         2              1   1.8
#>   4:     k1 2024-01-22  87.66189         2              1   1.8
#>   5:     k1 2024-01-29  88.19007         2              1   1.8
#>  ---                                                           
#> 100:     k1 2025-11-24 145.62487         2              1   1.8
#> 101:     k1 2025-12-01 146.31227         2              1   1.8
#> 102:     k1 2025-12-08 147.00154         2              1   1.8
#> 103:     k1 2025-12-15 147.69267         2              1   1.8
#> 104:     k1 2025-12-22 148.38568         2              1   1.8
compose_skill_index(tot, sh, "source", "skill", "week", w,
  base_period = c("2024-01-01", "2024-12-31"), type = "arithmetic"
)
#>       skill       week    indice n_sources covered_weight n_eff
